abstract.para: To configure &rear;, edit the /etc/rear/local.conf file to define your specific requirements, such as how to back up files and how to create and store the disaster recovery system. This configuration is sufficient for most systems. To re-create a non-standard system, you might also need to adjust the &rear; framework by editing the Bash scripts in /usr/share/rear/.

warning.title: Btrfs limitations
warning.para: Btrfs snapshot subvolumes can't be backed up and restored in their original state with file-based backup software.

Snapshot subvolumes on Btrfs file systems need almost no disk space because of Btrfs's copy-on-write functionality. However, file-based backup software backs up the snapshots as complete files, so they are included in the backup twice with their original file size. Therefore, the backed-up snapshots can't be restored to their original state.

step.para: Copy the closest matching &suselinux; example from the /usr/share/rear/conf/examples/ directory and paste it into /etc/rear/local.conf. Use this example as a starting point and adjust it for your specific system.

important.para: Currently, the latest example file is SLE12-SP2-btrfs-example.conf.

step.para: All &rear; variables and their default values are explained in /usr/share/rear/conf/default.conf. Examples of important variables are shown in the next steps:
Configure your file backup method with BACKUP and where to store the backup with BACKUP_URL. Use the following resources to learn more about configuring your backup method:

listitem.para: For a list of supported BACKUP methods, see man rear, section DESCRIPTION.
For more information about BACKUP_URL, see man rear, section BACKUP SOFTWARE INTEGRATION.
For more information about the additional options for each backup method, see the /usr/share/rear/conf/default.conf file.

example.para: Make sure the backup directory on the NFS server has the right mount options. For example, you might need no_root_squash because the rear mkbackup command runs as &rootuser;. For more information, see man exports.

step.para: Configure the boot method for the recovery system with OUTPUT and, if necessary, where to store the recovery system with OUTPUT_URL. If you don't specify an OUTPUT_URL, &rear; stores the recovery system at the location defined by the BACKUP_URL. Use the following resources to learn more about configuring your boot method:

listitem.para: For more information about OUTPUT and OUTPUT_URL, see man rear, section RESCUE IMAGE CONFIGURATION.
For more information about the additional options for each boot method, see the /usr/share/rear/conf/default.conf file.
